title: Automate PD/Slack Hooks with Tracing-Enriched Incidents, Runbook Templating & Postmortem Drafts
creator: Priya Nair
description: Goal: Reduce mean time to resolution and post-incident toil by automating the creation and enrichment of PagerDuty incidents and Slack channels using tracing hooks and runbook templates. Scope: (1) Add trace-derived context (span id, trace id, route, model_id, pod_id, latency buckets) to PD payloads; (2) Create a runbook templating service that instantiates versioned runbooks into a dedicated Git repo when an incident is created; (3) Auto-populate a postmortem draft in Confluence/Drive with incident metadata and initial timeline; (4) Support deduplication and suppression rules to avoid alert storms. Out of scope: rewriting PD routing policies or deep changes to PD escalation flows (will integrate with existing PD escalation configuration).
acceptance_criteria:
1) PagerDuty incidents created by observability pipeline contain the following keys in the payload: trace_id, span_id, affected_route, model_id, region, 95th_latency_ms, error_count.
2) A Slack channel is created with the incident number and pinned runbook link within 30s of PD incident creation.
3) A pre-populated postmortem draft exists in the team's Confluence space containing incident metadata, initial timeline (first 15 minutes), and links to traces/log queries.
4) Runbook templating supports versioning and can be edited by runbook owners; the created runbook commit appears in the runbooks repo.
5) Automated tests cover PD payload shape and runbook generation.
6) Canary rollout to infra-oncall team shows <5% false-positive rate and acceptable noise reduction compared to baseline.
tech_notes: Implementation sketch: (a) Add an enrichment middleware in the tracing ingestion pipeline that maps trace tags -> PD fields. The middleware will call a lightweight transformation service and sign requests to PD/Slack via service account. (b) Use a templating engine (mustache/handlebars) for runbook templates; templates stored in runbooks repo with metadata header (owner, severity, labels). (c) Postmortem drafts created via Confluence API using a minimal skeleton and an attachments list (links to traces and logs). (d) Use a Redis-backed dedupe window keyed by fingerprint (route+model+error_signature) to coalesce incidents. Security: service account keys live in KMS and rotate monthly. Auth: mTLS between pipeline and templating service.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Spike & Prototype): instrument enrichment middleware on staging traces (2 weeks). Phase 2 (Integration): PD/Slack API integration and runbook templating service with feature flag (3 weeks). Phase 3 (Canary): enable for infra-oncall only, monitor for 2 weeks, iterate. Phase 4 (Gradual rollout): enable by team tag in routing policy, monitor error/latency dashboards, full rollout after 4 weeks of stable metrics. Emergency rollback: disable feature flag and clear dedupe keys.
test_plan: Unit tests for payload schema and template rendering. Integration tests that mock PD/Slack and assert channel creation + runbook commit. End-to-end test on staging: generate synthetic high-latency trace -> verify PD incident + Slack channel + Confluence draft appear. Load test: simulate 1000 simultaneous alerts to validate dedupe window behavior. Monitoring: track incidents/sec, PD creation failures, template rendering errors, runbook commit latency.
monitoring_queries:
Suggested queries to validate behaviour:
- Failed PD webhooks: sum by(cluster) (increase_over_time(observability_pd_webhook_errors[5m]))
- Incident enrichment coverage: count_over_time(enriched_incidents_total[1h]) / count_over_time(raw_alerts_total[1h])
- Avg runbook generation latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(runbook_generation_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
- Trace-linked incident ratio: sum(enriched_incidents{has_trace="true"}) / sum(enriched_incidents)
